rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ 'Vector magnitude can be negative' ✅ Magnitude is defined as the absolute length, so it is always ≥ 0.  ·  ❌ 'Adding vectors is same as adding scalar magnitudes' ✅ Vector addition must account for direction using head-to-tail or component methods; only scalar magnitudes can be added algebraically.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **Vector:** A quantity having both magnitude and direction. Represented as arrow or bold letter: **a** or a⃗.  ·  **Scalar:** A quantity with magnitude only (mass, temperature, time).  ·  **Vector addition:** Triangle law: place tail of b at head of a; resultant closes triangle. Parallelogram law: diagonal from common tail.
